contentHtml:
This illustrative brief applies the UX standards to an internal customer directory. It is a design example, not a tested interface or a universal customer data model. Configuration and limitations are in the template README.

Context And Assumed Business Rules

An authorized support worker needs to create a customer record so colleagues can find it later, then correct contact details if necessary. Work is frequent on desktop and occasional on a small screen.

For this example only, the agreed rules are:

  • a display name is required to identify a record;
  • email and phone are optional contact methods;
  • email matches can identify possible duplicates but are not proof of the same person;
  • creating a record does not create a login or send a message;
  • archiving hides the record from the default active list and is reversible;
  • customer creation has a server operation identifier and status lookup;
  • edits use a version check to detect concurrent changes.

These are hypothetical product decisions. Validate them before applying the example to a real service. No user research or implementation test has been performed for this artifact.

Journey And Screen Choice

Search customers -> inspect possible matches -> create if needed
-> view confirmed record -> edit contact details -> confirm saved change

Start with one grouped form because the task is short and repeated. The page title is Create customer; brief supporting text explains that creation does not send an invitation. Reuse the application's existing form controls.

Field Purpose and status Input behavior
Display name Required for identification Text; accept common name characters and organization names
Email Optional contact method Email input; allow paste and explain invalid format on submission
Phone Optional contact method Telephone input; preserve meaningful international formatting

Do not ask for birth date, identity documents or address because the stated task does not use them. Mark optional fields in words. Use Create customer as the primary action and Cancel as secondary navigation.

Create Action Contract

Moment User experience System behavior
Submit Creating customer...; values remain visible Validate and submit with a stable operation identifier
Invalid input Summary linked to fields and specific messages No record created; preserve appropriate values
Possible duplicate Explain match and offer to inspect it Do not merge solely on the matching email
Confirmed create Record page states Customer created Show server-confirmed identity and persisted details
Server failure Explain failure and correction/retry route Restore usable controls; do not claim success
Response lost Explain that the result is not yet confirmed Query the operation before retrying with the same identifier

If the user inspects a possible duplicate, preserve their input so they can return. Display only records they are authorized to see. Any override or merge must follow the real application's permissions and business rules.

Editing And Leaving

Prefill current values and label the action Save changes. After a confirmed save, show the updated record and an accessible Changes saved status.

If a version conflict occurs, retain the user's draft and offer a comparison with the latest record. Do not silently overwrite. On meaningful unsaved navigation, offer Keep editing and Discard changes. There is no automatic browser-persistent draft in this example.

After returning to the list, preserve the previous search and filters. If the new or edited record does not match them, explain why it is not in the current results and offer a direct link to it.

Archiving

The action says Archive customer. Explain that it removes the customer from the default active list and can be reversed. Confirm the new state after the server response and provide a working restore path to authorized users.

This example does not authorize irreversible deletion. A different retention or deletion requirement needs its own consequence and recovery decisions.

Accessibility And Validation Plan

  • Associate labels, optional hints and errors with each input.
  • Move focus to the error summary on a failed multi-field submission.
  • Announce routine saving/result status without repeatedly moving focus.
  • Preserve logical keyboard order and readable reflow on a narrow screen.
  • Verify that repeated submission cannot create duplicate effects.
  • Exercise invalid input, lost response, permission failure and edit conflict.
  • Observe a representative worker creating and correcting a synthetic record without coaching, then ask what was saved and whether any message was sent.

Expected outcome: the worker can find the resulting record, explain the operation's actual effects and recover from a mistake. Record execution evidence separately; none is implied by this plan.
